name: Learn basic celestial navigation concepts
blurb: How sailors found their position for centuries: latitude from the angle of a star, longitude from precise time. Even the concepts are worth understanding.
gear: A sextant, or a homemade cross-staff or astrolabe
Nautical almanac data or an app
steps: Learn the core idea: measuring a celestial body’s altitude above the horizon, at a known time, gives you a line of position.
Learn latitude from Polaris, whose altitude in the northern hemisphere equals your latitude within a degree.
Learn the noon sight: the sun’s maximum altitude at local noon gives latitude with a simple correction for the date.
Learn why longitude requires accurate time, and why the marine chronometer was such a historic breakthrough.
Learn the corrections that make sightings usable: dip, refraction, semi-diameter and index error.
Take real sights over several days and compare your calculated position to a GPS reading.
tips: This is genuinely difficult and needs real practice, but the concepts alone reshape how you understand maps and time.
Never look at the sun through any instrument without proper filters.
proof: You establish your latitude from a Polaris or noon sight to within about half a degree.
